Here's the re-ranked recommendation, re-scored specifically for **drag-drop visual editor + asset shelf + games AND apps + web-now/mobile-soon**, with shader preservation as the tiebreaker. All checks reflect current 2026 status.

## Finalist scorecard

| Engine | Drag-drop editor | Asset shelf / prefab palette | Games | Apps | Web export | Native mobile | Your GLSL shaders | Maturity / lock-in |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **PlayCanvas** | ✅ Full in-browser scene editor | ✅ Asset panel + **Templates** (prefabs) + built-in **Asset Store** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ native (publish button) | ⚠️ via Capacitor/PWA wrap (no 1-click store) | ✅ **GLSL runs as-is** (WebGL2); optional WGSL for WebGPU | High. Engine MIT/open; editor SaaS but full export |
| **Unity** | ✅ Canonical drag editor | ✅ **The** prefab shelf + Asset Store | ✅ | ✅ | ⚠️ WebGL2 (WebGPU still experimental, heavy builds) | ✅ best-in-class native iOS/Android | ❌ **rewrite to HLSL/Shader Graph** | Very high; proprietary + runtime/licensing baggage |
| **Godot 4.6** | ✅ Scene tree + dock editor | ✅ FileSystem/asset dock + AssetLib | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ WebGL2 (no WebGPU web yet) | ✅ native, much improved in 4.5/4.6 | ⚠️ **port** to Godot's GLSL-like language | High; MIT, **zero lock-in** |
| **Needle Engine** | ✅ (uses Unity/Blender as the editor) | ✅ (Unity prefab shelf) → three.js runtime | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (three.js runtime, light builds) | ⚠️ PWA/wrap | ⚠️ via **MaterialX/Shader Graph** convert; raw GLSL not 1:1 | Medium-high; niche but active |
| **Triplex** | ✅ drag files into scene (2026) | ❌ no prefab "shelf"/store — it's a component workspace | ⚠️ you build systems yourself | ✅ (R3F apps) | ✅ (it's just your React app) | ⚠️ wrap | ✅✅ **100% — it *is* Three.js** | Low-med; editor young, no engine/systems |
| **GDevelop** | ✅ no-code editor | ✅ big built-in asset library | ✅ (2D, new 3D) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ native iOS/Android | ❌ custom GLSL still experimental/limited | Med; MIT engine |
| **Defold** | ⚠️ editor immature | ⚠️ limited | ✅ (2D/mobile) | ⚠️ | ✅ | ✅ great mobile | ✅ native GLSL, but Lua-centric | Med; free |
| **Construct 3** | ✅ browser editor | ✅ asset packs | ✅ (2D only) | ✅ | ✅ | ⚠️ wrap | ❌ no user GLSL beyond effect addons | Med; SaaS |
| **Bolt / Lovable / v0** | ❌ prompt-to-code, no scene canvas | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (web apps only) | ✅ | ❌ | n/a | Not a fit — AI app scaffolders, no drag+shelf game authoring |

## Ranked recommendation — pick and go

### 🥇 #1 — PlayCanvas
It is the only option that hits **every** primary requirement at once *and* keeps your shaders:
- Real **in-browser drag editor** with a true **asset shelf** (Asset panel + **Templates** = prefabs + a built-in **Asset Store** to drop in models/materials/scripts).
- Makes **both games and apps**, publishes to **web today** with one click; **mobile-soon** via Capacitor/PWA wrapping to the App Store / Play Store.
- **Your Refract Three.js/GLSL shaders survive** — PlayCanvas's `ShaderMaterial` takes GLSL directly on WebGL2 (and lets you add a WGSL variant later for WebGPU). This is the least-rework path of any full editor. A node shader editor is also in closed beta.
- Lowest friction to your current stack (JS + GLSL, browser-native), open-source engine so limited lock-in.

**Why over the rest:** Unity/Godot force a shader rewrite; Triplex has no shelf/engine; the 2D builders can't run your 3D shaders.

### 🥈 #2 (alternate) — Unity (optionally shipped to web via Needle Engine)
If you want the **strongest possible prefab shelf and the best native mobile** and are willing to redo the watch shaders: Unity is the canonical drag + prefab + Asset Store engine, makes games and apps, and has the best native iOS/Android pipeline. Two caveats: **Web is still WebGL2** (WebGPU experimental, builds are heavy) and your **GLSL must be rebuilt in Shader Graph/HLSL**. Use **Needle Engine** if you love Unity's editor but want a lightweight *three.js* web runtime and a slightly friendlier shader path (Shader Graph → MaterialX). Pick this only if long-term native mobile depth outweighs shader rework.

### 🥉 #3 (alternate) — Godot 4.6
The **free, zero-lock-in** choice with a genuinely good drag editor + asset dock, real games-and-apps range, and **native web + mobile** export (mobile got major 4.5/4.6 attention). Trade-offs: **no WebGPU on web yet** (WebGL2/Compatibility only) and your shaders need **porting to Godot's GLSL-like language**. Best if you want to own the whole stack with no vendor and don't mind reauthoring shaders.

**Bottom line:** Go **PlayCanvas** — it's the one environment that gives you drag-editing + an asset shelf, builds games *and* apps, ships to web now / mobile soon, and lets your existing GLSL watch-face shaders come along with the least rework. Keep **Unity** in your pocket if native-mobile depth later trumps shader reuse, and **Godot 4** if you want a fully free, no-lock-in fallback.
